To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ADNF-8 and ADNF-9 are neurotrophic and neuroprotective factors that can prevent oxidative stress-induced impairment in synaptic function.

a neurotrophic peptide, a growth factor, and a neurotrophin protect neocortical synaptic terminals against oxidative stress-induced impairment in glucose and glutamate uptake, and against oxidative stress-induced mitochondrial dysfunction.

a short neurotrophic factor, ADNF-9 (a fragment of activity-dependent factor), protects cortical synaptosomes against amyloid beta-peptie- and iron-induced oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and impaired glucose and glutamate transporter function.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of neuroprotective strategies to prevent the degeneration of cortical neurons in neurodegenerative disorders.
the hypothesis that neurodegeneration is a process initiated by alterations in the function of synaptic compartments.
understanding the mechanisms of neurotrophin-mediated neuroprotection, and developing new therapeutic agents for the treatment of Alzheimer's disease and stroke.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

neurotrophic factor(s) can protect cortical synaptic terminals from amyloid and oxidative insults by enhancing glucose and glutamate transporter functions, suppressing oxidative stress, and preserving mitochondrial function.
ADNF- 9 is an effective neurotrophic factor in the protection of synaptic function and mitochondria in cortical synaptosomes.

the neurotrophic factors, ADNF-9 and bFGF, are capable of protecting synaptosomes from oxidative stress and mitochondrial impairment, which may be a common feature of several neurodegenerative disorders.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
neurotrophic factor stimulation of local synaptic signaling pathways is a potential mechanism for neuroprotection.

neurotrophic factor treatment of cortical neurons in culture or in vivo can prevent cell death, while neurotrophic factor treatments of cortical neurons in cell culture or in vivo, or of synaptosomes in vitro can prevent synaptic dysfunction and degeneration.
the ADNF-9 peptide is a novel neuroprotective molecule that can act locally in the brain to suppress oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction and impairment of synaptic transporter function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
neurotrophic factor fragments can exert direct protective effects at the level of synapses, and that this may be a useful strategy for the design of neuroprotective drugs.
neurotrophic factor stimulation can exert direct synapto- and neuron-protective actions that are mediated by transcription-independent mechanisms.

neurotrophic signaling pathways can be activated locally in the synaptic compartment and that these local signaling pathways are capable of protecting synaptic functions against oxidative and excitotoxic insults.
